lore_summary.en: The lion hunter. The poet-king who rhymes his own legend. Bahram vanishes into the earth with his horse.
lore_summary.fa: بهرام گور که در دربار عرب بزرگ شده بود، تاج خود را با کشتن دو شیر پس گرفت. شکارچی بی‌همتا، عاشق‌پیشه و شاهی مبدل‌پوش بود که میان مردم می‌رفت تا حقیقت را بشنود. مرگش رازآلود بود — در باتلاق شکارگاه رفت و دیگر برنگشت، گویی زمین او را بلعیده.

scenes.body_en: Bahram Gur is the Shahnameh's most human king — the one who hunts, loves, laughs, and disappears into legend without a body to bury. He was sent as a child to the Arab court of Nu'man in the southern lands, raised among horses and desert skills while his father Yazdegerd reigned in Iran. When Yazdegerd died, the Persian nobles refused the boy raised abroad. They crowned another. Bahram rode back and settled the matter himself: two lions had been placed guarding his crown in an open field. He walked forward, killed both lions with his club, and put the crown on his own head. The nobles found no further objections.

His name means onager — the wild ass of the steppe — because no one hunted the way he did. There is a famous scene with a slave girl named Fitna who challenged him to pin a gazelle's hoof to its ear with a single arrow while riding at full gallop. He did it. She was unimpressed, calling it mere habit rather than skill. He threw her from his horse in fury. She survived, and spent years training a calf to carry her on its back up a staircase each day, adding weight as it grew, until it was a full-grown ox she could carry upstairs. When she showed Bahram what practice could achieve, he understood what she had been saying. He took her back. The chronicle uses their argument to ask what separates talent from discipline — and decides, quietly, that discipline wins.

He was also a king of disguises. He went among his subjects in common clothing to hear what they said about him and to judge without being judged. He went to India, to China, to places a king had no business going. He loved music and kept singers close. Seven princesses from seven kingdoms told him stories on seven nights — each story a different color, a different world, a lesson he could not have received from his ministers.

His death was in keeping with everything else. He was hunting onagers in the marshes — his own namesake quarry — and rode into the swamp after one and did not come back. No body was found. The earth took him the same way it takes a story: completely, leaving only the shape of where he had been.

battle.intro_en: Bahram Gur hunted lions with his own hands, rhymed his own legend, and vanished into a swamp without a witness. To face this gate you must hold the enigma of a king who made his own ending into myth.
battle.intro_fa: بهرام‌گور با دستانِ خودش شیر شکار کرد، افسانه‌ی خود را در قافیه آورد، و بدونِ شاهدی در باتلاقی ناپدید شد. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید معمایِ شاهی را نگه داری که پایانِ خود را به اسطوره تبدیل کرد.

battle.intro_tg: Баҳромгӯр бо дастони худ шер шикор кард, афсонаи худро ба қофия овард ва бидуни шоҳиде дар ботлоқе нопадид шуд. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд муаммои шоҳеро нигоҳ дорӣ ки поёни худро ба асотир табдил кард.

codex.title_en: The King Who Hunted Lions With His Own Hands
codex.title_fa: شاهی که با دستانِ خود شیر شکار کرد
codex.summary_en: Bahram Gur's defining characteristic in the Shahnameh is physical excellence combined with a refusal to let the court do for him what he could do himself. He hunted lions alone. He bet his throne against a challenge and won it personally. He composed poetry. The Shahnameh presents these as unified qualities — a king who inhabited his own life rather than delegating it. This is different from the chronicle's other models of good kingship (Anushirvan's systemic justice, Kay Khosrow's righteousness) and different from its models of bad kingship. Bahram Gur is his own category: the king who made himself a legend in his own lifetime.
codex.summary_fa: ویژگیِ مشخصه‌ی بهرام‌گور در شاهنامه برتریِ جسمانی همراه با امتناع از واگذاری آنچه می‌توانست خودش انجام دهد است. او شیر شکار کرد. شعر سرود. تخت را خودش در چالش برد. شاهنامه اینها را ویژگی‌هایِ یکپارچه ارائه می‌دهد.

codex.summary_en: Bahram Gur understood something that most kings in the Shahnameh did not: that the stories told about you are a form of power, and that you can participate in their construction while you are alive. He performed for his own chronicle. He hunted in ways that would be reported. He made wagers that would be remembered. The Shahnameh is the record of this performance and simultaneously an acknowledgment that the performance was genuine — he really did hunt those lions, really did compose those poems. The legend and the life were the same thing.
codex.summary_fa: بهرام‌گور چیزی فهمید که بیشترِ شاهانِ شاهنامه نفهمیدند: که داستان‌هایِ روایت‌شده درباره‌ی تو شکلی از قدرت هستند و می‌توانی در ساختنشان در زمانِ حیات شرکت کنی.

codex.summary_en: Bahram Gur disappears into a swamp while hunting and is never found. The Shahnameh records this plainly: he went in, no one saw him come out, no body was found. This ending — the king who made himself a legend vanishing without a witness — is the Shahnameh's final gift to Bahram Gur: a death as unmeasurable as his life. He did not die in bed. He did not die in battle. He went hunting and was gone. The absence of a body means the legend has no endpoint. It can continue indefinitely.
codex.summary_fa: بهرام‌گور در حالِ شکار در باتلاقی ناپدید می‌شود. هیچ شاهدی نیست. هیچ جنازه‌ای یافت نمی‌شود. این پایان — شاهی که افسانه‌ای از خودش ساخت و بدونِ شاهد ناپدید شد — آخرین هدیه‌ی شاهنامه به اوست.

codex.title_en: The King Who Is an Enigma
codex.summary_en: The Shahnameh places kings into legible categories: the just king, the reckless king, the king consumed by pride, the king destroyed by his own virtue. Bahram Gur does not fit cleanly into any of these. He was not particularly just in the administrative sense. He was not reckless. He was not consumed by pride. He was excessive — in pleasure, in physical display, in the energy he brought to everything — but his excess did not destroy his kingdom. The Shahnameh is honest enough to include him as a category that resists its own organizing principles.
codex.summary_fa: شاهنامه شاهان را در دسته‌بندی‌های خوانا قرار می‌دهد. بهرام‌گور تمیز در هیچ‌کدام جا نمی‌گیرد. شاهنامه به اندازه‌ی کافی صادق است که او را به عنوانِ دسته‌ای که در برابرِ اصولِ سازمان‌دهنده‌ی خودش مقاومت می‌کند شامل کند.

codex.summary_en: Bahram Gur is credited in the Shahnameh and in tradition with introducing rhyme to Persian poetry — or at least with being the patron of the tradition that developed it. Whether historical or legendary, this attribution matters: it connects a king famous for physical prowess with the development of the art form that the Shahnameh itself exemplifies. Bahram Gur, the lion-hunter, is also the ancestor of the literary tradition that produced Ferdowsi. The Shahnameh notes this without irony because it is not ironic: strength and beauty have never been opposites.
codex.summary_fa: بهرام‌گور در شاهنامه و سنت با معرفیِ قافیه به شعرِ فارسی — یا حداقل با حمایت از سنتی که آن را پروراند — منتسب است. این انتساب اهمیت دارد: شاهِ معروف برای توانایی فیزیکی با هنری پیوند می‌خورد که خودِ شاهنامه نمونه‌اش است.

codex.summary_en: The swamp death of Bahram Gur became, in the tradition the Shahnameh records, not a death but a disappearance — which is a different thing. Disappearances can mean return. They leave room for the figure to persist in imagination. Alexander died with his hands open, his body visible. Bahram Gur left no body, no witnessed moment, no definite ending. In the Shahnameh's world, a king who controls his own ending — even by making it uncontrollable by others — has performed the final act of the legend he spent his lifetime building.
codex.summary_fa: مرگِ بهرام‌گور در باتلاق به جای مرگ ناپدید شدن است — که چیزِ متفاوتی است. ناپدید شدن می‌تواند یعنی بازگشت. شاهی که پایانِ خودش را کنترل می‌کند — حتی با کنترل‌ناپذیر ساختنِ آن برای دیگران — آخرین عملِ افسانه‌ای را انجام داده که عمرش را صرفِ ساختنش کرد.
